record.name: Ivona Bogdanović
record.title: Full Professor
record.bio: Ivona Bogdanović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Chemical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad (2000, 2003) and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2008, with a doctoral thesis on fouling layer formation during ultrafiltration of whey protein concentrates. Following a postdoctoral stay at the Faculty of Food Technology and Biotechnology in Zagreb (2009–2010), she returned to Novi Sad and progressed through the academic ranks to Full Professor in 2021. Her group investigates membrane separation processes with emphasis on fouling mechanism characterisation in protein-rich bioprocess streams, cleaning-in-place protocol development, and transmembrane pressure management for ultrafiltration and microfiltration applications. She teaches Membrane Processes and Unit Operations in Chemical Engineering at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. The group operates a dedicated membrane filtration laboratory equipped with cross-flow ultrafiltration rigs, a bench-scale CIP test station, an atomic force microscope for foulant surface characterisation, and inline turbidity and conductivity monitoring instrumentation.

joint projects with bioprocess, dairy, or plant protein companies
equipment access (cross-flow ultrafiltration rigs, AFM, bench-scale CIP test station)
student internships in the membrane filtration laboratory

record.industry_experience: Bogdanović has conducted contract research for two regional dairy processing companies on CIP protocol optimisation for installed ultrafiltration lines. She has provided technical consulting to a fermentation start-up regarding membrane selection for broth clarification at pre-pilot scale.
record.notes: Bogdanović has a strong preference for collaborations that involve access to authentic industrial process streams rather than model solutions alone, as her group considers industrially realistic feed complexity essential for meaningful fouling studies. She is particularly interested in connecting with companies processing plant-based proteins or operating fermentation downstream processing lines.
